data.description:
## Description

**What**: Add a required CI check that scans the merged-tree state of `.test-index` for unresolved RED markers and blocks the session→main merge when any are present. Named under an always-runs umbrella job so branch protection can require a single stable check-context name. The scan reflects the cumulative session state at the point of merge (NOT just session-branch HEAD), so cross-sub-PR RED-marker resurfacing is caught.

**Why**: Today RED markers in `.test-index` can reach main because no CI required check enforces them at the session→main boundary. With cumulative session branches (multiple sub-PRs landing on one session branch via S1), the scan must reflect cumulative state — not just the most recent sub-PR's diff.

**Scope**:
- IN: New umbrella required-check (or umbrella job added to an existing workflow) that scans `.test-index` on the merged-tree state; behavioral test asserting the check blocks a RED-marker push; integration with branch protection (the required-check naming).
- OUT: Adding the check to branch protection itself (handled by the cutover-migration story); RED marker addition or removal logic (existing test gate).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, a CI required-check named under an umbrella job (e.g., `merge-pipeline-checks/red-test-blocker`) scans `.test-index` on the MERGED tree (the result of the would-be session→main merge) and exits non-zero if any unresolved RED markers are present.
  ← Satisfies: "A required CI check scans .test-index for unresolved RED markers and blocks session→main merge"

- When this story is complete, the check is registered under an umbrella job with a stable check-context name (does not change across branch-filter conditional executions). Branch protection can require this single name and have it always reportable.
  ← Satisfies: "named under an umbrella job for stable branch-protection"

- When this story is complete, a behavioral test (`tests/workflows/test-red-test-blocker-merged-tree-scan.sh`) opens two sub-PRs on the same session branch — one that removes a RED marker, one that re-introduces it — and asserts the merged-tree scan blocks session→main merge.
  ← Satisfies: Red team Finding #11 (merged-tree scan, not session-HEAD-only)

- When this story is complete, the epic's own sprint attempts a RED-marker push to main and is blocked by the check (verifying SC4(a)'s sprint-fixture verification).
  ← Satisfies: "epic sprint's attempted RED-marker push is blocked"

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic.
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done requirement

## Considerations

- [Correctness] The scan target MUST be the cumulative session state, not session HEAD or the last sub-PR's diff. A naive scan that only looks at the diff of the session→main PR would miss RED markers re-introduced by an earlier sub-PR.
- [Sequencing] S4 must run AFTER S5's version-bump commit (if S5 sequencing chooses bump-before-final-review). Otherwise S5's bump could touch `.test-index` indirectly via test-quality side effects, and S4's check would pass against a stale state.
- [Migration] Adding this required check via branch protection will block in-flight session→main PRs that haven't run the new check yet. The cutover-migration story owns the branch-protection rollout; this story only registers the check.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO operator, session->main merges are blocked when unresolved RED test markers remain in .test-index
